title: The Craziest Pirates in History
description:
A rich man who bought a pirate ship with zero sailing experience, an Irish pirate queen who talked her way past Elizabeth I, a redbeard who became an admiral, two women who out-fought their crew, a tea-drinking captain with injury insurance, a pirate who got knighted, and Blackbeard's smoking hat: seven of the craziest pirates in history, counted down from seven to one. Every story is real, and we flag the legends when we tell them. Chapters are added automatically.

#history #pirates #blackbeard #funnyhistory #historypros

beats.say: In May 1718, four pirate ships parked right outside Charleston, one of the richest ports in the American colonies.
Their captain was Blackbeard, the most feared pirate of his day.
He grabbed ships, took hostages, and sent the town's leaders a ransom demand.
What does he want? Gold? Silver?
Medicine. A whole chest of it.
And he got it. That's not even the strangest thing a pirate ever did.
Today we're counting down seven of the craziest pirates in history. Blackbeard is number one.

show.sub: Seven pirates. All real. Mostly ridiculous.

show.title: The Gentleman Who Bought a Pirate Ship

beats.say: Number seven: Stede Bonnet, the man who bought his way into piracy.
Bonnet was a rich landowner on Barbados, a British island in the Caribbean. He had a sugar plantation, a wife and kids.
What he didn't have was any sailing experience. None at all.
In 1717 he decided to become a pirate anyway. Nobody really knows why.
Most pirates stole their ships. Bonnet bought one with his own money, and he named it the Revenge.
Then he hired about seventy men and did something almost no pirate did: he paid them wages.
Gentlemen, you will receive a regular salary.
A salary? For piracy?
He captured a few ships along the American coast. Then, in the Bahamas, he met Blackbeard.
You don't really know how to sail, do you?
I have a very nice ship.
Bonnet was wounded and his crew was restless, so Blackbeard took over the Revenge. Bonnet stayed on Blackbeard's ship as a guest.
He was caught in 1718 and hanged in Charleston. Turns out money can buy a pirate ship, but not pirate skills.

show.title: The Pirate Queen Who Met the Queen

beats.say: Number six: Grace O'Malley, the pirate queen of Ireland.
She was born around 1530 into the O'Malleys. The clan ruled a stretch of coast in the west of Ireland.
Her family lived off the sea: fishing, trading, charging passing ships for safe passage, and sometimes robbing them.
Grace commanded her own ships for decades, which was almost unheard of for a woman back then.
By the 1590s, England was tightening its grip on Ireland. An English governor, Sir Richard Bingham, captured her son and her half-brother.
So in 1593, in her sixties, Grace sailed to England to ask Queen Elizabeth the First herself.
Your governor took my son. I want him back.
And what does England get?
My ships will fight your enemies.
Legend says they spoke in Latin. It also says Grace blew her nose on a royal handkerchief and tossed it in the fire. That's probably just a good story.
But the result is in the records: Elizabeth ordered her family released. A pirate walked into her enemy's palace and walked out with a win.
Number five: Barbarossa, the pirate who ended up running a navy.
In the early 1500s, two brothers from the Greek island of Lesbos became corsairs, sea raiders of the Mediterranean.
They ended up fighting for the Ottoman Empire, the great Turkish empire based in Istanbul, against Spain and its allies.
Europeans called them both Barbarossa. That's Italian for Redbeard.
In 1516, they captured Algiers, in North Africa, and turned it into their base.
Oruç was killed fighting the Spanish in 1518. His younger brother, Hayreddin, took over, and took the nickname too.
He raided Spain and Italy again and again. So in 1533, Sultan Suleiman, the Ottoman ruler, made him grand admiral of the whole navy.
Congratulations. The navy is yours.
All of it? Even the big ships?
In 1538, Spain, Venice and the Pope sent a huge Christian fleet to finish him. They met at Preveza, off Greece.
Barbarossa had about one hundred twenty galleys. Counts vary, but the other side had far more ships.

show.label: The Battle of Preveza
show.sub: Barbarossa's galleys vs the Christian fleet (counts vary)

beats.say: He still won. Today, a former pirate has a big statue by the water in Istanbul.
Number four: Anne Bonny and Mary Read, two women who fought harder than their whole crew.
Anne was born in Ireland and grew up in South Carolina. She moved to the Bahamas and joined the pirate Calico Jack Rackham.
Mary was born in England. The earliest account says she spent years dressed as a man, and even served as a soldier in Flanders.
That account comes from a 1724 book, A General History of the Pyrates, and historians can't confirm most of it.
In October 1720, a pirate-hunting ship caught Rackham's crew off Jamaica.
According to that book, most of the men were drunk and hid below deck, while Anne and Mary kept fighting.
Come up and fight like men!
Cowards, the lot of them!
They were captured anyway. Rackham was sentenced to hang, and the book says Anne visited him one last time.
She was sorry to see him there, but if he had fought like a man, he need not have been hanged like a dog.

show.text: Sorry to see him there, but if he had fought like a man, he need not have been hanged like a dog.
show.who: Anne Bonny to Calico Jack, in A General History of the Pyrates (1724)

beats.say: Both women were sentenced too, but both said they were pregnant, so their executions were put on hold.
Mary died of a fever in prison. Anne simply vanishes from the records. Nobody knows what happened to her.
Number three: Bartholomew Roberts, better known as Black Bart, the most successful pirate of the age.
He was born in Wales around 1682, and spent years as an ordinary, honest sailor.
In 1719, pirates captured his ship off West Africa, and he joined them. Weeks later, their captain was killed, and the crew voted Roberts in.
Yes, pirates voted. Many crews elected their captains, and could fire them too.
In about three years, Roberts captured more than four hundred ships, from Canada to Brazil to West Africa.
He wasn't a typical pirate. He wore fine clothes, and by many accounts, he drank tea instead of rum.
His crew signed strict written rules, called articles.
Lights out at eight o'clock. And no gambling for money.
Is this a pirate ship or a boarding school?
The rules even paid out if you got hurt. Lose a limb, and you got eight hundred pieces of eight, which were Spanish silver coins.

show.label: Payout for losing a limb
show.sub: pieces of eight, from the shared fund

beats.say: That's basically injury insurance, long before most workers had anything like it.
According to the 1724 book, his motto was this.
A merry life and a short one shall be my motto.

show.text: A merry life and a short one shall be my motto.
show.who: Bartholomew Roberts, in A General History of the Pyrates (1724)

beats.say: It came true. In 1722, a Royal Navy warship caught him off Africa, and he was killed in the battle.
His crew buried him at sea in his finest clothes, just as he'd asked.
Number two: Henry Morgan, the pirate who got a knighthood.
Morgan was another Welshman. In the 1660s, he was in Jamaica, an English colony in the Caribbean.
England's big rival there was Spain, which owned the richest colonies in the Americas.
Morgan was a privateer: basically a pirate with a permission slip from the government to attack England's enemies.
He raided Spanish towns in Cuba, Panama and Venezuela, and got very rich.
In 1671 he led more than a thousand men through the jungle. Their target was Panama City, one of Spain's richest towns.
The city burned down, and Morgan's men carried off loot, though less than they'd hoped.
One problem: England and Spain had just signed a peace treaty. So Morgan was arrested and shipped to London.
You attacked Spain in the middle of a peace treaty.
Nobody told me about any treaty, Your Majesty!
Instead of being punished, he was knighted in 1674. Then he was sent back as lieutenant governor of Jamaica, the island's number two official.
And his new job? Hunting pirates.
Later, a popular book described him as a cruel pirate. He sued the publishers for libel, meaning lying in print, and won two hundred pounds.
He died in Jamaica in 1688, rich and respected. The pirate ended up writing the rules.

show.title: The Man With the Smoking Hat

beats.say: And number one: Blackbeard, the pirate who turned his own face into a weapon.
His real name was probably Edward Teach, and he was likely born in England.
In 1717 he captured a big French ship, added more cannons, and renamed it Queen Anne's Revenge.
He had a huge black beard, twisted into little braids tied with ribbons.
And the 1724 book says that in battle he tucked slow-burning fuses under his hat. Those are the cords used to fire cannons.
Imagination cannot form an idea of a fury from hell to look more frightful.

show.text: Imagination cannot form an idea of a fury from hell to look more frightful.
show.who: "Captain Charles Johnson", A General History of the Pyrates (1724), on Blackbeard

beats.say: The look did the work. There are no known accounts of him harming his captives. Ships just gave up.
That brings us back to Charleston in 1718. His ships blocked the harbor for about a week.
Send me a chest of medicine, or the hostages don't come back.
Medicine? Fine! Just please go away.
The town paid, and the hostages came home, minus most of their fancy clothes.
A few months later, Royal Navy Lieutenant Robert Maynard cornered him at Ocracoke, an island off North Carolina. Blackbeard died in the fight.
His pirate career lasted only about two years. His legend has lasted three hundred.
And in 1996, divers found the wreck of Queen Anne's Revenge off North Carolina.
Honorable mention: Ching Shih, who led tens of thousands of pirates in China, then retired with a pardon. She's in our badass women video.
And notice what you didn't see today: walking the plank. Historians have found only a handful of real cases. Most of it comes from later stories.
That's the list: a gentleman who bought his ship, a pirate queen, a redbeard admiral, two fearless women, a tea drinker, a pirate knight and a smoking hat.
Which pirate was the craziest? Tell us in the comments.
